# Figure 8

**Source**: Figure 8 of the [paper](../paper.pdf), as identified in the inspection text below.

**Caption**: Reported runtime against sample size and dimension on logarithmic axes. (paraphrase; original caption is preserved in the source PDF).

**Screenshot**: [figure8.png](figure8.png)

**Figure type**: quantitative_plot

**Extraction method**: digitized_estimate

**Reading confidence**: medium

**Axes**: Sample size or dimension and seconds; both axes logarithmic.

## Visual description

Type quantitative_plot, two panels, BOTH x and y axes logarithmic. Left x sample sizes250,500,1000,2000,4000; right x dimensions1,10,100,1000,10000. Y seconds, displayed ticks10^-2 through10^2 with some plotted points below10^-2. Eleven-method legend as Figure1. Means and standard deviations over ten repetitions are stated; error bars are present. Caption left fixed dimension10; right fixed sample size500; default, method-specific permutation counts and AutoML60-second training limit.

Visually FUSE lies below MMDAgg; left FUSE times are roughly ≈0.015,≈0.05,≈0.2,≈0.8,≈4 seconds; MMDAgg roughly ≈0.03,≈0.09,≈0.3,≈1.4,≈7 seconds. These are approximate chart readings and must never be substituted for the local 574.510456007-second whole-run measurement. Near-linear methods are faster at large sample size; optimization-based curves have large nearly fixed costs. The right panel repeats the left panel's shapes and magnitudes, with ME's last point absent, matching the demonstrated plotting-code source error in §5.3. Preserve it as the published figure and flag its asserted dimension interpretation; do not silently correct or claim independent dimension-scaling evidence. Method digitized_estimate/visual_description; confidence medium for plotted values, low for the intended dimension experiment's underlying provenance.

## Trend summary
The left-panel source supports an increasing cost with sample size under its named defaults. No dimension-scaling conclusion is attributed to the duplicated published RHS. The local whole-container measurement includes sampling, compilation and logging and is not compared to these warmed per-test timings.
